institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew that SciencesPo Paris would offer some great learning experiences with cutting edge research and engaging professors.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy as I could gather all the information I needed from other students at home who had been abroad (at SciencesPo).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you are Danish, I would recommend the groups on social media specifically for Danes in Paris. They are helpful!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very important to engage with the surroundings

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to spend some time figuring out how the system worked. There were a lot of different portals to apply through and documents to send.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to spend some time figuring out how the system worked. There were a lot of different portals to apply through and documents to send.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I knew that I could contact the Erasmus office for guidance if I needed it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very different from my home university. It was stressful to fight against time for the remaining vacant spots so I ended up taking some courses that I didn't know existed before the registration process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to ally yourself with a person who has been through it before when registering.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ended up having other courses than expected

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were only for MA students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some elements were alike and some were different. I noticed that it really depended on the personality and preferences of the professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Grand Strategy in Diplomacy Past and Present, Macrohistory, Business & Human Rights, Comparative Political Economy: Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, The Limits of Political Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Grand Strategy in Diplomacy Past and Present

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My computer burnt out.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some groceries varied drastically in price and a good tip is shopping locally and trying to go for products manufactured in France to avoid tolled goods.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, but I din't part-take

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: People should enjoy

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed going to the many, many museums of Paris and enjoying the life of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had an easy time adjusting because I had previous experiences with living abroad.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make sure to join the various whatsapp groups for information regarding social events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The French are generally open to you if you speak French whereas most Danes are perfectly capable of speaking English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love France and Paris, especially the culture of going out every day to socialize with friends and acquaintances.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take a French course, leave your housing and go out in the afternoons/evenings, use the various whatsapp networks to gather recommendations.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get used to a more hands-on approach where control and protocol play larger roles.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really achieved great experiences with my professors and enjoyed the feeling of having been well-prepared by UCPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making connections to the "locals". Paris can be a tough place to get to know the inhabitants as they do tend to prefer their own French-speaking kind. Make an effort!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
